summary: Maxton tower on Drummond Island, Chippewa County, Michigan: 100-foot CCC-era tower erected 1936, standing by 1937; no source found describing it today.

events.note: June 1936 newspaper items report the 100-foot tower being erected by CCC crews near Maxton; a later June 1936 item says it would be built that summer by CCC crews from Camp Moran
September 1937 newspaper item describes a child climbing the 100-foot Maxton fire tower, so the tower was standing by then

notes_for_editor: Built and first-standing dates rest on 1936-1937 newspaper items reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page. The June 1936 items describe the design two ways (stairway ladder type; steel); neither is confirmed elsewhere, and both say 100 feet. The record height of 30.5 m is the 100-foot figure converted. The TopoQuest entry is a name database; it does not prove the structure remains. Two web searches found nothing on the tower after 1937 and nothing on fires or staffing. The 1936 towerman's cabin was a plan; no source names a towerman. Lead: Lake Superior State Forest (Sault management unit) records.
